title: The spherical perceptron with bi-orthogonally invariant disorder
main_claim: For bi-orthogonally invariant A_N (M=floor(alpha N)) whose singular-value empirical law converges to a compactly supported nu with no outliers, and bounded continuous f, the spherical perceptron pressure F_N(A,f) converges in probability and in mean to F_{alpha,nu}(f). This limit is the mesh limit of sup_rho {1/2 sum v_i log(rho_i/v_i) + alpha P_p^f((s_j^2 rho_j/alpha)_j)}, where the angular pressure P_p^f comes from a Gaussian Stiefel-cascade variational formula G_{theta,p} with a shared coordinate, one-sided Haar-flag witness penalties, and theta -> 0.
coverage: Checked: radial decomposition, i.e. output radius a_j = s_j^2 rho_j N/M, the Dirichlet(n_i/2) rate via Stirling, and v_j = alpha p_j with the null block 1-alpha. Checked J_p as (p/2) times the Marchenko-Pastur log-determinant, which equals (1/2) int_0^p log(1-u) du, and the H_p shell entropy. Checked the operator-norm Lipschitz bound and the C_b truncation. Proposition aspect: verified the Beta moment E V^{-(M-2)/2} = Gamma(N/2)/(Gamma(M/2)Gamma(1+k/2)) and the ball comparison constant e^{4b}. Canonical Lemma: verified coercivity with Q = I + sign(C)/2, the comparison giving Psi <= 0 at C = -(B0+1)I, and the exact entropy-Hessian identity numerically for k = 2..8. Checked the Schur/compressed-inverse step at the freezing level and the envelope argument. Upper bound: checked the r=0 contact lower bound and the GG fluctuation rates. Lower bound: checked the GG rates (s_M = M^{3/8}, s = M^{-1/8}), the IBP sign in c_j + tr B_{j,d} = int tr(q b), and the shell-difference / Psi-J cancellation algebra leading to S(q*) + 1/2 sum w tr((q-q*)b). Only spot-read: matrix-symmetry/synchronization via GG, the conditional-variance step of the bulk lemma, the Haar majorization lemma, the penalty/soft-duality section, and the edge-interval appendix.
sibling_notes: The family-222 board already had an entry for this same dir (rank194 no_gap_found from an earlier pass). That pass numerically verified the canonical duality, the majorization transport and the shell bookkeeping, and noted one minor point: a cascade-pressure second derivative written as a plain Gibbs variance. I independently concur and have overwritten the entry with a second-pass summary. The companion papers (scalar spherical, Ising, jamming) were all marked no_gap_found. This paper says it uses no theorem from the scalar companion, so there is no circular dependence.
